subject: Item Factor Analysis - Unable to replicate Mplus

messages.author: 3fa278f261d60ce4
messages.subject: Item Factor Analysis - Unable to replicate Mplus
parts:
I am estimating a single factor model containing 14 observed variables, each with 3 response categories.

In both my lavaan and Mplus syntax I am treating them as ordered variables and employing theta parametrization. Additionally, I am freely estimating all factor loadings and fixing the latent variance and mean to 1 and 0, respectively. I have also specified each program to execute listwise deletion to ensure that the same analytic sample is being used across programs. But differences result.

The number of free parameters are 14 (lavaan) and 42 (mplus) and this difference is due to lavaan not reporting SEs for any of the item thresholds (14*2 = 28). Why are no SEs available for the lavaan model (see output attached) even though unstandardized and standardized estimates are available? No warnings/errors were produced by either program.

There are also differences in estimates across programs with respect to factor loadings (both standardized and unstandardized), item thresholds, and scales for y*.

Below are the specifications and abridged output from both programs (I tried to attach these files, but got an error message).

Any insights on why I am observing these differences would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks!
-Graham

pcString <- '
pc =~ PC1_1 + PC1_2 + PC1_3 + PC1_4 + PC1_5 + PC1_6 + PC1_7 + PC1_8 + PC1_9 + PC2_1 + PC2_3 + PC3_1 + PC3_2 + PC3_3

pc ~~ 1.0*pc
pc ~ 0*1
'

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Item Factor Analysis - Unable to replicate Mplus
parts: The number of free parameters are 14 (lavaan) and 42 (mplus) and this difference is due to lavaan not reporting SEs for any of the item thresholds (14*2 = 28).

It is related to that, but not caused by it.  When you use the base lavaan() function rather than the sem() or cfa() wrappers, you only estimate the parameters explicitly specified in your model syntax.

pcString <- '
pc =~ PC1_1 + PC1_2 + PC1_3 + PC1_4 + PC1_5 + PC1_6 + PC1_7 + PC1_8 + PC1_9 + PC2_1 + PC2_3 + PC3_1 + PC3_2 + PC3_3

pc ~~ 1.0*pc
pc ~ 0*1
'
m.pcFit <- lavaan(pcString, data = analyticSamp, ordered = pcItems, parameterization = "theta", mimic = "mplus")

You could set auto.th = TRUE (which is what the sem() and cfa() wrappers do) or specify your thresholds in the model syntax to set them free in your model.
